checks.finding: Terms, env var semantics (SDD_PANELIST_TIMEOUT parsing/defaults), exit-code taxonomy, and the per-runtime escalation table are concrete enough that independent implementers would converge on the same observable behavior. No unresolved vague term found that would produce divergent, test-passing implementations, beyond the item captured under EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE (which is a test-coverage gap rather than a text-clarity ambiguity, since the literal POSIX kill-to-single-pid reading is unambiguous on its own terms).

The attempt-1 BLOCKED contradiction (PowerShell table calling Kill($true) 'not a second mechanism' while Edge Case 7's counterpart presupposed a soft-request stub) is resolved: requirements.md:60 now states plainly 'No soft-request step precedes it, and none is to be added,' and acceptance-tests.md:66-70 states the PowerShell suite 'carries no (b) sub-case' without describing any stub behavior inconsistent with that. BL-004's dual-runtime parity constraint is explicitly reinterpreted as outcome-level parity rather than mechanism-mirroring, which reconciles rather than conflicts with the asymmetric escalation table. No other direct conflict found between requirements, acceptance criteria, constraints, or non-goals.

requirements.md:57-60 and acceptance-tests.md:64-72 add a 'no orphan of any child the stub spawned' assertion to the PowerShell (a) sub-case only, justified by Kill($true)'s tree-kill semantics. The identical risk applies to POSIX: the table's POSIX row specifies only SIGTERM/SIGKILL to a single stored pid with liveness checked via 'kill -0 <pid>', and TEST-004(a)'s POSIX sub-case asserts only that the stub's own PID is dead, not that any descendant it spawned is gone. Edge Case 2 states the general orphan risk but is satisfied by 'the child is gone' -- the immediate child only. Downstream failure: a POSIX implementation using the literal, natural reading of the table (signal to the stored pid alone, no process-group targeting) would pass every stated acceptance test while leaving a vendor-CLI-spawned grandchild process orphaned holding a live API session -- precisely the class of defect the spec explicitly engineered a PowerShell-only test to catch. This belongs at spec review because it is a Phase-1 acceptance-test gap, not an implementation defect: BL-004's parity requirement and the spec's own 'not simply less covered' framing invite a symmetry check that fails in the POSIX direction here.

All three listed Assumptions are resolved or explicitly bounded: the SIGTERM-termination assumption is paired with a required escalation test (Edge Case 7 / TEST-004(b)); the install.sh citation's provenance gap is disclosed with the load-bearing claim shown to rest independently on a first-hand command -v result; and the file:line staleness risk is addressed by an explicit re-verification instruction. All three prior investigation Open Questions (rate-limiting, MCP checklist authority, residual-risk placement) are resolved by name in AC-002, AC-013, and AC-014 respectively, not left dangling.

No human approval, governance, or irreversible-change boundary is introduced by this feature. The only waiver reference ('unless the task is explicitly waived', INV-005) describes pre-existing check-cross-model behavior that BL-002 explicitly keeps unchanged; this feature adds no new approval gate. No such boundary is in scope, so SKIP applies.

Aside from the scoped item captured under EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE, the specification gives implementation-policy review concrete exit codes, env-var semantics, a per-runtime mechanism table, a full edge-case list mapped to specific tests, and resolved open questions -- it does not require a design reviewer to invent core product behavior.
